Text.Text: It's done, then. The forge answers to iron again, and every robe on this rock has to wonder if the spear behind them learned from you. Rule the last: a doctrine is only clean while someone keeps it clean. That's you now. Go be inconvenient to sorcerers.
You've got nerve. Now get your Spear training to rank 50. Nerve won't catch a blade, and the people I hunt know it.

Six Forcebane adepts have taken my counters into the Forge Caverns and sold them to the people they were meant to stop. Put the six down and bring me their heat ledger. I want names. Especially the names wearing robes.
Take the key to the Forge Caverns entrance in the Sith Fortress forgeworks. Keep your spear ready. Nobody down there is going to thank you for coming.

Rule one, and carve it somewhere you'll see it: reach ends ritual. A sorcerer needs a breath to call the storm down. A spear crosses four meters in less. Forcebane isn't mysticism, it's arithmetic with a point on the end. Timing, distance, iron. The forge decides whether your arithmetic holds when the other side cheats.
Go to the Sith Fortress forgeworks on Korriban. The entrance to the Forge Caverns is there; my key opens it. Bring your company up to the entrance together.

Smiths who trained as soldiers and pray like Sith. The adepts fight in pairs and they don't break when the first one drops. Keep your point moving, kill the chanting ones first, and don't let the forge floor pick your footing for you.
Six Forcebane adepts in the Forge Caverns. Their heat ledger comes back here to the Valley Temples.
Forge-smoke on your coat and ash on your hands. Let's see it, then.

Look at these rosters. They're not training a class, they're training a market. Every name in here paid in Sith script. Clean work; the credits are yours. Rest the arm, you'll want it. This goes deeper.

Five specialists are hardening blades with a Sith tempering matrix. They used to ask me where to put the point. Now they're making sure no one else can. Beat the five in the caverns and bring that matrix here.
Back into the caverns. Don't stand admiring the steel while someone decides where to put it.

A quench-frame. You seat a blade in it while the alloy sets, and whatever the frame holds, the steel remembers. Mine held angles and timing. Theirs holds Sith alchemy, so the metal remembers hate instead. If that sounds like mysticism to you, it is, and that's exactly why I want it on my bench and not theirs.

That's the question with a knife in it. Somebody who drilled under me is standing down there in better robes, drawing my forms on their chalkboards. The ledger's rosters were student handwriting. I trained maybe a dozen people who could teach this. The matrix will tell me which one turned.

Specialists don't drill in pairs, they drill with an audience of apprentices who join in uninvited. Expect the fight you planned plus half of one you didn't. Kill the specialist first and the audience remembers other appointments.
Five specialists in the caverns have the tempering matrix. Put them down and bring it here.
That box under your arm is humming. Good sign. Worse sign for them.

There it is. My angles, scored into a Sith quench-frame like scripture. I'll burn the imprint out tonight. You're not a stranger anymore, so hear this plain: what's past the tempering line doesn't fight fair, and I'm going to ask you to go there anyway.

The warden's keeping the Forge Caverns shut to anyone who objects. Challenge him there. When he's down, bring me the anvil sigil he wears. Take friends if you've got them; a spear only reaches so many throats at once.
The Forge Caverns challenge marker calls the warden. Recruit help first if you can. Last lone hunter I sent came back in a crate. I'd like the sigil without having to fold your spear beside it.

He was the first one the turncoat trained, and the best. The sigil says the deep forge answers to him: quench lines, apprentices, all of it. He's felt every form I teach coming since before you learned to hold a spear level. That's what different means. Nothing you do will surprise him. Do it anyway, in numbers.

Bait draws the commitment, blade punishes it, net closes the escape. Good work for hunters who trust one another. The warden learned all of it. I'd find people who can keep him busy while you put the point where it belongs.

Past the tempering line the floor is slag channels and the light is whatever's burning. The warden likes it there because crowds don't follow. Be the crowd anyway. And if he offers to let your friends leave so long as you face him alone, that's not honor, that's him doing arithmetic too.
The Forge Caverns challenge marker calls the warden. Beat him and bring me his anvil sigil.
The hammering stopped two nights ago. The whole ridge noticed. That was you.

Cracked. Good. The warden's gone and my watchers say the apprentices have noticed. Take your pay. The overseers who remain will know your name now; let that make them careless before it makes you proud.

Four overseers signed off on this little school. They hold the clearance token in the caverns. Put the four down and bring it back. We'll see how eager their customers are when there's nobody left to vouch for the steel.
Bring the clearance token here. I'd like their customers to have one reason less to call this honest work.

Two smiths, a quartermaster, and a duelist who thinks she's my equal. All four drilled under the turncoat, which means all four drilled under me, once removed. They know my forms the way you know your own signature. So don't write your signature down there. Write something new.

Every crate of tempered blades leaving that forge carries the token's stamp, and the buyers pay on the stamp, not the steel. Take the token and the trade is paper. Their buyers are Sith, and Sith don't forgive missed deliveries. I'm not just ending a school. I'm arranging its creditors.

They'll try to cover each other, with the duelist waiting for you to overextend. Pick your reach carefully. Bringing help wouldn't shame you; fighting outnumbered just to be proud would waste a good spear.
Four overseers in the caverns still have the clearance token. I want it when they're finished.
You're standing straighter. That's what killing a circle does. Show me.

Four names I trained, once removed, closed out in a week. The stamp still smells of ink. They were clearing a shipment when you arrived. That's the trade dead, the school headless, the buyers furious. All that's left is the man who taught them, and that one I have to talk about sitting down.

The master is in the Champion Forge. Use the challenge marker and call him out. He knows every counter I taught, so don't offer him the fight he's expecting. Beat him, then come back to the temples. I'll want to hear where you put the point.
That's the last order I have. Call him in the Champion Forge. When he's down, come stand here again. I want to hear it from you, not from the watchers.

My net-man. Bait, blade, and net, and he was the net, the one who closed doors. Best timing I ever hunted beside. When you face him, that's what you're fighting: every escape you'd use, already closed. He'll ask about me. Tell him I kept the rules. He'll know which one I mean.

Don't fight the duel he offers you. Watch the exits, hold your reach, and make him commit before you do. With help, give him different angles to answer. He'd prefer you trying to prove you can take him alone.

The forge heart is his temple now. Heat that bends your sight, one bridge over the crucible, and him at the middle of it, patient as an anvil. Nobody walks off that bridge alone, so don't walk onto it alone. And he will talk. He talks better than I do. If your feet stop moving while he does, your friends are carrying you home.
Call the master at the Champion Forge challenge marker. Beat him, then find me here at the temples.
The watchers went quiet, then came the smoke, then you, walking like a man with nothing left to prove. Say it anyway. I've earned hearing it.

So he had an answer for my counters, and you had an answer for him. Good. Take the pay. If you're ready to learn Forcebane, plant your feet. We're starting with the thing a robe can't make you forget.
Go over the job again.
Six adepts. One ledger. I'll get it done.
Why a spear against Force users?
How do I get into these caverns?
What's waiting in there besides adepts?
Not today.
The Forcebane Forge Heat Ledger. Six adepts stopped arguing about it.
Run the second job past me again.
Five specialists. I'll bring the matrix back whole.
What is a tempering matrix?
How did your counters end up on Korriban?
How do the specialists fight?
Give me a day first.
One Forcebane Sith Tempering Matrix, warm off the rack.
Tell me about the warden again.
I'll hunt the warden.
What makes this warden different?
Why bait, blade, and net?
What's it like past the tempering line?
Let me find people I trust first.
The Forcebane Cracked Anvil Sigil. He didn't want to part with it.
Walk me through the circle again.
All four. And the token comes home.
Who are the four?
What does the token actually clear?
How will they come at me?
Let me sharpen up first.
The Forcebane Overseer's Clearance Token. The circle's signatures are done.
Tell me about him once more.
I'll put him down.
What was he to you?
How do I beat the man who wrote the rules?
What happens at the heart of the forge?
Not yet. Not until we're ready.
It's finished. The master is dead, and the doctrine is yours again.
